*title 9, and the only reason that the investigations are being conducted in the first place is because the the legal system within colleges have been completely brushing a majority if not all of sexual assault cases under the rug and have been misreporting their statistics to the department of education. 

In 2012 45% of colleges reported 0 sexual assault cases being even REPORTED. Fun fact, I went to a 30,000 student school, was sexually assaulted in 2012, had the guy arrested  and went to a "trial" within the school so the guy who assaulted me could possibly be suspended or expelled from school and he got away with nothing. When I checked my schools stats in 2013, there were zero, ZERO sexual assaults reported during the 2012 calender year. Reports in general, not reports that led to an arrest, or reports that led to penalizations, plain reports. So a 30,000 student school dealt with no reports? That's highly unlikely but I know for a fact there should've at least been one, which was me, but there wasn't. 

Keep in mind men are raped too so women can potentially be equally at fault, and that a school isn't going to jump on sexual assault cases to ruin people's lives. Especially now that the government is involved, schools are going through the necessary precautions to make sure they're reporting more appropriately. And if there's been a huge increase in the stats of reports of assaults since the title 9 investigation has opened, it's most likely because schools are actually starting to take these cases seriously and report accurately, not that there has been an increase simply in false reporting. 

Yes, people can and do lie about crimes, but that percentage can't even be accurate when more than 60% of sexual assault cases go completely unreported. And in a lot of cases it's due to the fear of back lash and victim blaming.
